samples.question: The picture shows exactly two black cords of equal thickness lying on white paper; each cord runs from one edge of the paper to another and bends only at right angles. Wherever the two cords meet, one cord passes over the other: the cord that passes underneath is hidden near the meeting point, so it shows a short white break there, and it continues on the far side of that break in the same straight direction. Following a cord means walking along it and passing straight through its own breaks, but never stepping onto the other cord at a meeting point. Three round beads - one red, one green, one blue - sit on the cords; exactly two of them are on one and the same cord. Which two beads lie on the same cord: red and green, red and blue, or green and blue?
